prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on what you want from Branson.

Quick decision guide
- Want walkable access to shows, restaurants, nightlife? Stay in a hotel on/near the 76 “Strip” or Branson Landing.
- Want lake views, privacy, or an outdoors/Ozarks getaway? Rent a cabin/Airbnb on Table Rock Lake or near Indian Point/Hollister.
- Traveling with kids who want a waterpark/resort experience? Pick a family resort (Great Wolf Lodge or Big Cedar).
- Want luxury and spa/amenity-heavy stay? Choose Chateau on the Lake or Big Cedar Lodge.
- On a tight budget? Budget motels on 76 or an entire/ private-room Airbnb can save money.

Best places by traveler type (specific recommendations)

1) For convenience, shows, restaurants (couples or first-time visitors)
- Hilton Promenade (Branson Landing) — on the Landing next to shops, dining, lakefront fountain show; walkable to downtown attractions.
- Margaritaville Resort Branson — newer, resort vibe at the Strip area with good on-site dining and pool.
- Branson hotels on the 76 Strip (Best Western Plus, Comfort Inn, etc.) — practical, close to theaters.

2) For families with kids
- Great Wolf Lodge Branson — indoor waterpark resort; very kid-focused.
- Big Cedar Lodge (nearby in Ridgedale) — family activities, lakeside, plenty for kids and adults; higher-end but great for multi-generational trips.

3) For luxury, lakefront or romantic escapes
- Chateau on the Lake Resort, Spa & Convention Center — upscale lakeside resort with spa and scenic views.
- Big Cedar Lodge — luxury cabins, golf, spa, private activities.

4) For Silver Dollar City / theme-park access
- Stay west of town near Highway 76 toward Silver Dollar City (Hollister/Indian Point area) — lots of cabins and vacation homes/Airbnbs within 10–15 minutes of the park.
- Look for private cabin rentals or condos marketed for Silver Dollar City guests.

5) For a quieter Ozarks/cabin experience
- Table Rock Lake cabins through Airbnb or Vrbo — private docks, firepits, great for boating and fishing.
- Small cabin rentals near Indian Point or Hollister for a quieter stay but still within driving distance of shows.

6) Unique/interesting options
- Keeter Center (College of the Ozarks) — well-regarded, quietly upscale and near historic downtown Branson.
- Stone Castle Hotel & Conference Center — themed, family-friendly option near the Strip.

Airbnb vs hotel — pros/cons (short)
- Airbnb pros: more space, kitchen, privacy, better for groups/families, lakeside/cabin options, often better value for multi-night stays.
- Airbnb cons: variable quality, extra cleaning fees, minimum-night rules (especially during Silver Dollar City season), less consistent service, sometimes tricky parking or check-in.
- Hotel pros: predictable service, daily housekeeping (if you want it), on-site amenities (pool, restaurants, concierge), often located where you want to be (the Strip/Branson Landing).
- Hotel cons: smaller rooms, higher per-person cost if you need multiple rooms, can be more expensive for big groups.

Practical tips
- Book early for peak seasons (summer, holidays, major events) — Branson fills up fast, and Silver Dollar City has lots of weekend traffic.
- If you’ll be doing lots of shows, staying on/near the Strip saves driving and parking time.
- If you want a lake experience, prioritize listings that explicitly mention docks and boat parking.
- Check cancellation policy, cleaning fees, and whether the Airbnb is a full place vs private room.
- Consider renting a car — many Branson attractions are spread out.

If you tell me your travel dates, group size, budget, and priorities (shows vs lake vs kids vs nightlife), I can give a tailored short list of specific hotels or cabin neighborhoods and example Airbnb search filters.
